From: rafael_mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.ai>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Nora Patel <nora@finserv-pay.com>
Date: 2027-04-12T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Investigation results: inter-tenant replay causing duplicate token billing (details + remediation)

Hi all,

Investigation summary: we confirmed duplicated ingestion for a ~36 hour window (2027-03-30T02:00Z -> 2027-03-31T14:00Z). Root cause: a migration job that re-tagged an existing staging API key as part of a tenant consolidation inadvertently left a staging copy active. That staging copy had been included in an automated re-router, so identical requests were forwarded to both the new production entity and the legacy staging entity; both entities were billed independently.

What we measured:
- Duplicate request_ids found: 17,842 (sample attached: duplicate-token-extract-20270412.csv).
- Duplicated token delta (estimated): 1,138,450 tokens -> gross overage charge €18,960.
- Affected models: text-generation (gpt-like v1), and streaming embedding endpoints.

Recommended remediation and next steps:
1) Retroactive credit for duplicated tokens: we propose to apply a full credit for the duplicated token quantity (~€18,960) to the March invoice.
2) VAT treatment: because the duplicated events were recorded under two EU legal entities, we recommend issuing a corrected invoice with reverse-charge notation removed for the duplicated portion and reflect it on the corrected ledger; legal/tax should sign off, but the corrected invoice will reduce FinServ's VAT liability.
3) Permanent fix: enforce API-key isolation by entity (runbook linked below) and add a duplicate-requestid drop-signal in the ingest pipeline (quick mitigation patch deployed to staging; prod scheduled this week).
4) Evidence bundle: attached CSVs and a filtered trace slice (internal link).

Timeline: credit processed within 3 business days after confirmation; corrected invoice within 7 business days; production dedupe rule deployed by 2027-04-15.

Links and runbooks: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/BILL-782 (investigation ticket); https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example (evidence bundle).

Let me know if you want us to proceed with the credit + corrected invoice now, or if FinServ requires a DocuSign amendment for VAT handling.

Regards,
Rafael Mendes
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: duplicate-token-extract-20270412.csv, trace-snippets.txt

From: Nora Patel <nora@finserv-pay.com>

Rafael — thanks for the thorough analysis and the evidence bundle. We agree with the root cause and the proposed remediation.

Finance is comfortable with the proposed credit: please proceed with a provisional 60% credit immediately and the remaining 40% after we confirm the corrected invoice and VAT treatment with our tax counsel. Our legal team requests a short DocuSign amendment to confirm VAT reclassification for the corrected invoice; please send that through and we'll review.

Final ask: can you confirm the deployment ETA for the dedupe rule and provide a short note we can include with our internal tax filing explaining why the duplicate events were never valid taxable events? A one-paragraph justification from your side would be perfect.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Nora Patel
Head of Billing Ops
FinServ Payments
